summary_paragraph: A 45-year-old man with advanced HIV/AIDS and recent history of toxoplasmosis and respiratory failure was admitted from a rehabilitation facility with fever, tachypnea, and altered mental status. He was found to have ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, confirmed by sputum and urine cultures, and was treated with cefepime. His respiratory status improved, and he was successfully weaned from mechanical ventilation to trach mask support. Treatment for ongoing cerebral toxoplasmosis was continued, with MRI showing stable lesions and reduced edema. Thrush was treated with fluconazole, and CMV/HSV pneumonia prophylaxis was maintained with valganciclovir. His hospital course was complicated by transient hyponatremia and bladder outlet obstruction, both managed conservatively. He was discharged to extended care with plans for follow-up in infectious disease and neurology clinics.
